location: picture overlay pills (feed name, Output/Source picker, timecode, REC) over bright picture areas
issue: Overlay text on glass pills loses contrast over bright video: primary label 3.21:1 and secondary 1.98:1 over a bright window region. Both are below the WCAG 4.5:1 minimum for 11–12 pt text. The 52% glass has no guaranteed backing.
evidence: kit.css .glass rgba(44,44,48,0.52) + --label 0.88 / --label2 0.56; computed over #dfe9ee (the scene's window) = 3.21 and 1.98; over mid-tone wall = 7.40. The Feed 1 pill sits on the bright window in main-expanded/single.
scenario: A presenter by a bright window or a white wall can't read 'REC 12:31' or the Output/Source label on the picture they're watching.
recommendation: Give picture overlays a guaranteed scrim: a darker capsule (≈ 75% black under the glass) or a top/bottom gradient scrim, and keep primary-weight text only. Spec says overlays stay dark in Light mode; add a minimum-contrast rule (≥ 4.5:1 against white video).
alternatives: Edge gradient scrim (top 56 pt, bottom 44 pt) behind all overlays
Move timecode and REC into the strip and keep only the identity chip on the picture

issue: The sidebar camera rows show on air vs next only as a red or green dot, with no text. Red vs green differ by luminance ratio 1.68, so they're indistinguishable with protan/deutan color blindness. The pictures carry text badges; the sidebar doesn't.
evidence: r3.js sidebar(): tally = '<span class="dot red">' / '<span class="dot green">'; row text is only '2160p 59.94 · REC 12:31'. Computed red #ff453a vs green #30d158 = 1.68:1.
scenario: A red-green colorblind operator uses the sidebar to check which camera is in Program and reads both rows as the same.
recommendation: Add the role word to the row subtitle ('On air', 'Next') or a shaped glyph (filled dot vs ring), matching the strip badges. VoiceOver label: 'Feed 1, on air in Program, recording'.
alternatives: Use the same text badge component as the collapsed strip
Show a small 'ON AIR' pill on the row and drop the dot

issue: Effect chips show on vs off only by tint: blue-tinted with light-blue text vs grey with tertiary text. Off-chip text is 2.46:1 and there's no shape, icon or text difference. Collapsed chips are 9.5 pt.
evidence: r2.css .fx span / .fx span.on; r3.js fxChips(small) font-size 9.5px; computed label3 on fill2 = 2.46. Only bypass adds strikethrough.
scenario: In a meeting, an operator with low vision or color deficiency can't tell whether the LUT chip is on, so they don't know what Zoom is getting.
recommendation: Encode state with shape: filled chip plus a checkmark for on, outlined or hollow for off. Raise off-chip text to secondary (≥ 4.5:1) and minimum 10 pt. Give each chip a VoiceOver label: 'LUT on'.
alternatives: Show only enabled effects as chips ('LUT · 1080p · 4:2:0') as plain text
Toggle-style capsules (native Toggle .button) whose on state is shown by fill and checkmark

location: tertiary text (.c3, .k2 labels, '—' values, shortcut hints, 'ProRes 422 · clean source', 'Not published')
issue: Tertiary label color measures 2.5–2.65:1 on every surface (window, card fill, sidebar glass, dropdown), yet it carries real information: section labels (AUDIO, RECORDING), shortcut hints (⌃2), codec/source note, 'Not published', 'Not in use'. That fails WCAG 1.4.3 for informational text. Light mode is worse (secondary 3.5:1, tertiary 1.85:1).
evidence: Computed: label3 on window 2.65, on fill 2.56, on sidebar 2.53, on dropdown 2.57; light label2 3.50, label3 1.85. r3.js: 'ProRes 422 · clean source', cut-button '⌃n' hint in c3; .k2 uses --label3 (r2.css).
scenario: A user with mild low vision can't read 'Not published' or the recording format; in Light mode secondary values like time left and file size become hard to read.
recommendation: Reserve tertiary for decoration and disabled state. Informational values (time left, size, codec, published state, section labels) use secondary or primary. Rely on the system's Increase Contrast and test both appearances. Spec §2 should state 'no essential information in tertiary'.
alternatives: Promote section labels to secondary semibold caption
Drop low-value tertiary text entirely (e.g. 'ProRes 422 · clean source' can live in the ⋯ popover)

location: small badges and role pills ('On air in Program', 'ON AIR', 'Next', default badges)
issue: Several status badges miss 4.5:1 at their size: red badge text on tinted red 3.97:1, white on the 92% red role pill 3.60:1, default grey badge 3.84:1. Collapsed-strip role badges drop to 9.5 pt. These badges are the non-color backup for tally, so their legibility matters more than usual.
evidence: Computed: badge.red #ff6961 on rgba(255,69,58,.2)=3.97; role.air white on #ff453a@92% over video=3.60; badge default=3.84. main-collapsed.html collapsed badges 'height:16px;font-size:9.5px'.
scenario: Glancing at a collapsed strip mid-meeting, the operator can't read the tiny 'On air' badge, and the red tint alone doesn't disambiguate from REC.
recommendation: Badges minimum 10.5 pt semibold. Use a darker red fill (systemRed at 100% with white bold text measures ≈4:1 — use bold 13 pt or a dark text on lighter red) or keep the tinted style but with primary text color. Verify with Increase Contrast.
alternatives: Use text-only role labels in primary color with a colored leading dot
Make the ON AIR pill a solid tally light and put the words beside it

location: tally rings on pictures (red on air, green next, orange paused/skipped)
issue: The rings have low contrast against typical video: red 1.62:1, green 2.72:1, orange 2.68:1 vs a mid-tone scene, all below the 3:1 non-text minimum. Red vs orange luminance differs only 1.66:1, so paused (orange) and on air (red) rings look alike. Text badges rescue the pictures, but the ring is presented as the primary signal in the legend.
evidence: r3.css .onair::after inset 4px red, .next::after 3px green; computed vs #7a6553. states.html uses an orange ring for 'Skipped by Auto' and paused (standalone).
scenario: A protan user sees Feed 1 (on air, red ring) and Feed 2 (paused, orange ring) as the same dark outline; only the small badges differ.
recommendation: Add a contrasting inner and outer hairline (white 1 pt inside, black 1 pt outside) to every ring so it reads on any video. Distinguish states by pattern as well as hue (solid = on air, dashed = cutting/queued, double = paused). Keep the badge mandatory. Spec §7 already plans ring 4 → 5 pt under Increase Contrast; add the hairline by default.
alternatives: Move tally into a solid tally bar above the picture (broadcast-style) instead of a ring over video
Reserve rings for Program only; show paused/skipped only in the badge

location: hover-only controls: picture hover group (Freeze, Clean, Zoom, Detach), collapsed strip hover (Pause, Stop), Four Up hover toolbar
issue: Several controls appear only on pointer hover, with no keyboard focus reveal or VoiceOver path defined. Spec §7 defines a Tab order but doesn't say hover-revealed controls appear when focus enters the picture or strip, and there's no keyboard way to reveal the collapsed strip's Pause/Stop besides expanding.
evidence: four-up legend 5: 'At rest only the name, state, timecode and REC stay visible'; main-collapsed legend 2: 'Hovering a collapsed strip reveals its inline controls'; spec §7 keyboard bullet has no focus-reveal rule.
scenario: A keyboard-only or Switch Control user can't freeze a picture or pause one feed's recording in Four Up without the mouse.
recommendation: Rule: anything revealed on hover is also revealed when keyboard focus or VoiceOver focus enters the container, and stays exposed to accessibility at all times (accessibilityElement children always present, hidden only visually). Every hover action also has a menu command and a context-menu item (already true for Freeze/Clean; add Pause/Stop Recording for the focused feed).
alternatives: Show hover controls permanently at reduced opacity when 'Full Keyboard Access' is on
Put Pause/Stop for the focused feed in the Record menu with ⌘R / ⌥⌘P

location: live-control hit targets: strip chevron (18 pt), Processing switch (28×16 pt), collapsed record button (30 pt), cut-key badges, ⋯ (24 pt)
issue: Some live controls are under the 24 pt minimum from the audit plan. The expand chevron is 18×18. The strip Processing switch is a mini switch 16 pt tall, and toggling it mid-meeting bypasses the whole pipeline. The off switch track contrast vs window is 1.65:1 (mockup rendering).
evidence: r3.css .strip3 .chev 18px; kit.css .switch.sm 28×16; r3.js strip(): '<div class="switch sm on">' beside fx chips; computed fill3 track vs window 1.65.
scenario: Using a trackpad during a call, the user misses the 18 pt chevron and hits the adjacent Processing switch, bypassing effects in Zoom.
recommendation: Minimum 24×24 hit area for chevron and ⋯ (padding, not glyph size). Use a regular or small native switch with a text label ('Processing') rather than an unlabeled mini switch beside chips. Keep ≥ 8 pt spacing between disruptive and benign controls.
alternatives: Move Processing into the ⋯ popover and the toolbar/menu (⇧⌘B), leaving the strip with read-only chips
Make the whole collapsed strip header the disclosure target (click name area to expand)

location: text below 10 pt: collapsed effect chips 9.5 pt, collapsed role badges 9.5 pt, shot timer and timeline labels 9.5 pt, k2 section labels 10 pt
issue: Informational text is set at 9.5 pt in collapsed strips and timeline marks, below the macOS minimum readable size (Apple uses 10 pt caption2 as the floor). It doesn't scale with the system text-size setting.
evidence: r3.js fxChips small 'font-size:9.5px'; main-collapsed.html/program-view.html .marks 9.5px; r2.css .shot .mkl 9.5px; .k2 10px.
scenario: On a 13-inch display at default scaling the collapsed chips and cut-reason labels are unreadable without leaning in.
recommendation: Floor at 10 pt (caption2) for any information; use semantic text styles (.caption2) so the macOS text size setting and accessibility zoom apply. If collapsed rows can't fit, drop chips rather than shrinking them.
alternatives: Replace collapsed chips with a single 'Effects 3/4' label
Show chips only on hover/expand

issue: The VoiceOver plan labels elements but defines no announcements for live events that a non-visual or eyes-elsewhere user must hear: cut happened or queued, recording started/stopped/failed, signal lost, disk low, Auto skipped a source. Continuously changing values (elapsed time, timecode, meters at 2 Hz) risk chatty output if exposed as live regions.
evidence: spec.html §7: labels for pictures, meters 'updates throttled to 2 Hz for speech'; no mention of AccessibilityNotification.Announcement or which events announce.
scenario: A blind or low-vision presenter relying on VoiceOver isn't told that Feed 1's recording stopped after a source error until they explore the strip.
recommendation: Add an announcement table to spec §7: announce state transitions only (Recording started/stopped/failed, Cut to Feed 2, Signal lost on Feed 3, 12 minutes left on 8TB), priority high for errors. Never auto-announce timers or meters; expose them as values read on focus.
alternatives: Optional 'Speak status changes' setting in General
Mirror announcements as system notifications when the app is in the background

issue: Light appearance is shown only for one channel column, the dropdown top and the status bar (spec §8). Sidebar, ⋯ popover, Settings, menus, states, diagnostics and tool popovers are dark-only. The light sample's own secondary text measures 3.5:1 on #f5f5f7.
evidence: spec.html §8 .light overrides; computed light label2 rgba(60,60,67,.62) on #f5f5f7 = 3.50, label3 = 1.85.
scenario: A user in Light mode gets an untested sidebar where glass over a bright wallpaper washes out secondary text.
recommendation: Round 4: render the main window (sidebar + strips + status bar), the ⋯ popover and one dropdown in Light. Check secondary text on glass over a bright wallpaper. Rely on system colors in code.
alternatives: Add a light/dark toggle to the mockup kit so every page can be viewed both ways

location: picture click-to-cut and focus semantics for assistive tech
issue: The picture has three meanings on click (cut, focus tile, select feed), and its VoiceOver element is described as one element with a label. The default VoiceOver action (VO-Space) on a picture is undefined: would it cut Program? An accidental activation by an AT user would cut a live meeting.
evidence: spec §7: 'one element per picture'; main-expanded legend 2: 'Click a picture or press ⌃1/⌃2 to cut'; monitor-tools: focus by click.
scenario: A VoiceOver user navigating pictures presses VO-Space to hear details and cuts Zoom to the wrong camera.
recommendation: The picture's default accessibility action is 'Focus' (non-destructive). Cutting is a named custom action ('Cut to Feed 2') and a separate button, never the default. Aligns with fixing S1 for everyone.
alternatives: Expose 'Cut' only via the cut buttons and ⌃n; pictures have no activation action

issue: The proposed red recording dot and orange attention dot on the menu bar icon are tiny color-only marks (red vs orange 1.66:1 luminance difference). They're indistinguishable for many color-blind users and invisible against some wallpapers on a transparent menu bar.
evidence: menubar.html icon states card; settings General 'Show recording dot / attention dot'; main-expanded menubar markup: 6×6 px dot.
scenario: A deuteranopic user can't tell whether the dot means 'recording' or 'problem'.
recommendation: Differentiate by symbol, not hue: recording = video.fill with a small filled circle badge; attention = exclamationmark.triangle badge (or a distinct SF Symbol variant). Template image so it adapts to menu bar appearance. accessibilityLabel states the full status (already noted).
alternatives: Swap the whole icon to record.circle while recording and to exclamationmark.triangle on attention

location: recording vs paused vs stopped states on the record button and REC pills
issue: Paused vs recording is distinguished mostly by color (red vs orange) on the dots in sidebar rows and collapsed strips. The red/orange pair differs by 1.66:1, while the round record control's recording vs idle (square vs circle) is a good shape cue.
evidence: standalone sidebar rows 'dot red' vs 'dot orange'; four-up collapsed Feed 4 'dot orange' + 'Paused 04:12' text; computed red vs orange 1.66.
scenario: In Four Up, a color-blind user skims the dots to confirm every camera is rolling and misses the paused one.
recommendation: Pair the paused dot with a pause glyph (⏸) instead of a plain orange dot; text is already present in most places — make the glyph the rule in compact contexts (sidebar, dropdown rows, status bar).
alternatives: Use SF Symbols record.circle.fill / pause.circle.fill everywhere instead of dots

location: Reduce Transparency / Increase Contrast / Reduce Motion coverage
issue: Spec §7 covers Reduce Transparency for glass and overlays, Increase Contrast for rings and separators, and Reduce Motion for meters and REC. It omits the shot timer progress, the director timeline 'now' line, cut transitions and popover/sheet animations. Increase Contrast doesn't address the low-contrast tertiary text or the badges.
evidence: spec.html §7 lines on Reduce Transparency, Increase Contrast, Motion.
scenario: With Reduce Motion on, the shot timer still animates continuously in the sidebar.
recommendation: Extend §7: under Reduce Motion, shot timer and timeline update in 1 s steps without easing; under Increase Contrast, tertiary text → secondary, badges get 1 pt borders, effect chips get outlines, overlays get opaque capsules.

issue: Sidebar secondary text on the floating glass measures 4.70:1, marginal for 10.5–11 pt captions. Tertiary measures 2.53:1. Contrast depends on the wallpaper behind the translucent sidebar, so a bright wallpaper will push secondary below 4.5:1.
evidence: computed label2 on sidebar glass (rgba(48,48,52,.6) over a dim wallpaper) = 4.70; label3 = 2.53. Sidebar captions use 10.5 px (r3.css .sb3 .mini-row small).
scenario: With a light wallpaper, sidebar rows such as '12:31 · 27.5 GB · ProRes 422' and '1 h 35 m left' fade.
recommendation: Keep sidebar captions ≥ 11 pt secondary; rely on the system sidebar material (which adapts its tint) rather than custom translucency; verify against a white wallpaper.

issue: From the accessibility side: red covers on air, REC, the record/stop control, errors and destructive buttons. Red vs orange (paused/warning) differs by luminance 1.66:1 and red vs green 1.68:1, so hue carries too much meaning for color-blind users. Text badges exist on pictures but not in the sidebar, menu bar dots or effect chips.

Always-visible tool buttons are 24×28 pt, adequate as targets, but crowd text pills over bright video (L6-01). Moving them to hover reveal must come with a keyboard and VoiceOver reveal rule (L6-07), otherwise decluttering costs accessibility.
evidence: r3.js tile() tool group height 24, min-width 28; four-up hover-only variant.

issue: Fixed px text with 9.5–10 pt floors and nowrap rows means the macOS text size setting or accessibility zoom will overflow or clip strips. No layout rule exists for larger text.
evidence: L6-09; .strip3 .r white-space: nowrap (r3.css).

issue: For assistive tech the risk is worse: the picture's default activation is undefined and could cut Program (L6-12).
evidence: spec §7 single picture element; legend 'Click a picture … to cut'.
